I'm Madhusudan, an applied statistician. I trained as a computer science engineer and came
to statistics through the work. I started with randomised evaluations, moved on to causal
questions where nobody had randomised anything, and now design methods for official
statistics, where the job is turning messy administrative records into numbers people can
rely on.

Most of what interests me sits where those meet: working out cause and effect when you
can't run the experiment, dealing with data that is missing or wrong, and taking location
seriously when where something happens is part of the answer. When there is a choice, I lean Bayesian.

I started BetterCallStats to write these things down properly. My test for whether I
understand a method is whether I can explain it from its assumptions, show the maths, and
back it with code that runs. Each post is an attempt to pass that test. Where it helps,
small examples run in your browser, so you can change a number and see what moves.

If you're new here, start with [Alphabets of Causality](../posts/alphabets_causality/index.qmd),
the first post in a series on causal inference.

If you spot a mistake or see something differently, I'd like to hear it. Message me on
[LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/in/madhusudan-chunletia-83a623210) or open an issue on the
[blog's repository](https://github.com/Bettercallstats/blog/issues).
